The passage says the Eagles should not be intimidated by big names, so they appeared timid and goal-shy.
Debutants are players taking part in the World Cup for the first time, so first-timers.
The writer says the hope of going beyond the first round is very much alive, so he is optimistic about the Eagles.
The moralist and the economist hold positions that are at variance with each other.

The passage shows that morality and religion lead to economic problems, so they are somewhat interconnected.
The writer says a growing number of alcohol consumers and smokers appear to take to drinking and smoking.
The moralist regards smoking as a sign of moral degradation, so smoking is bad and unacceptable.
